gameplayPillars.title: Daily life and relationships
gameplayPillars.description: The calendar system makes time a resource: school, Social Links, activities, social-stat growth, and evening options compete for limited days and time slots.

gameplayPillars.title: Tartarus and turn-based combat
gameplayPillars.description: Battles emphasize elemental weaknesses, One More turns, Shift actions, Theurgy attacks, party roles, and Persona skills while Tartarus provides the main dungeon progression.

gameplayPillars.title: Persona fusion and growth
gameplayPillars.description: The protagonist can hold multiple Personas, fuse them into new forms, inherit skills, register them in the Compendium, and build specialized combat setups.

record.worldSummary: The game takes place primarily around Tatsumi Port Island, Gekkoukan High School, Iwatodai, and the supernatural Dark Hour. Tartarus is a towering labyrinth that appears during the hidden hour after midnight.

storyChapters.title: Arrival in Port Island
storyChapters.body: A transfer student arrives in Port Island, experiences the Dark Hour, awakens Persona power, and becomes involved with S.E.E.S.

storyChapters.title: The Dark Hour and S.E.E.S.
storyChapters.body: S.E.E.S. explores Tartarus and confronts Shadows while trying to understand the Dark Hour and the unusual events affecting the city.

storyChapters.title: Confronting mortality and fate
storyChapters.body: The story increasingly focuses on mortality, grief, bonds, personal responsibility, and the consequences of the group’s discoveries.

features: Daily calendar and Social Link progression
Turn-based combat with Shift and Theurgy systems
Persona fusion and customization
Modernized visual presentation and UI
Additional scenes and voiceover
Large DLC catalog including Episode Aigis
record.perfNotes: Nintendo Switch 2 launch version targeted 30 fps. Patch 1.03 added a 60 fps Performance Mode for docked/TV play and corrected inconsistent frame pacing. Digital Foundry reports only small dips from 60 in that mode; handheld remains 30 fps.

handheld.notes: Handheld remains at 30 fps after patch 1.03; frame pacing was improved by the patch.

tv.notes: Patch 1.03 adds a 60 fps Performance Mode in docked/TV mode with small dips from target in measured testing.

devicePerformance.performanceNotes: Performance data reflects patch 1.03 testing. Input latency remains a noted issue in Digital Foundry’s analysis.

record.storageNotes: Nintendo Europe lists a 21.7 GB download. Physical copies are Game-Key Cards and require downloading the game data; package notices can require additional free space beyond the listed download size.

faq.q: Does Persona 5 Royal work on Nintendo Switch 2?
faq.a: Yes. Nintendo lists the game as compatible with Nintendo Switch 2, but it runs as the Switch version rather than a native Switch 2 Edition.
The main game is single-player. Nintendo lists some online-supported functionality, but there is no cooperative or competitive multiplayer campaign.

faq.q: Why is there no DLC purchase type even though 40+ DLC items are listed?
faq.a: Nintendo states that the Switch release already includes more than 40 previously released DLC items. The supplier data also contains only two variants, so the storefront correctly keeps only Standard Offline and Standard Online product types.

record.perfNotes: Switch targets 30 fps. Backward-compatibility testing on Switch 2 reports a much steadier 30 fps and significantly shorter loading. Approximate ~864p docked / ~648p handheld figures come from secondary technical reporting, so they are explicitly marked as reported rather than official Nintendo measurements.

handheld.resolution: up to 1080p TV-profile rendering with Handheld Mode Boost; 720p without Boost
handheld.outputResolution: 1920x1080 display output with Handheld Mode Boost
handheld.notes: Backward compatibility stabilizes the 30 fps target noticeably compared with original Switch in testing.

tv.resolution: up to 1080p dynamic, system-upscaled to 4K output
tv.notes: Backward-compatible 30 fps with improved consistency; no native higher-frame-rate patch.

devicePerformance.upscaling: System-level upscaling to 4K output in TV mode
devicePerformance.loadingNotes: RPG Site testing reports dashboard-to-game loading around 20–21 seconds on Switch 2 versus roughly 40–42 seconds on original Switch, and save-related loads around 7–8 seconds versus roughly 18–20 seconds.
devicePerformance.sourceName: RPG Site / Nitchigamer / Switch 2 Handheld Mode Boost testing
devicePerformance.performanceNotes: Backward compatibility materially improves frame-rate stability and loading. Before Handheld Mode Boost, Switch 2 handheld uses the fixed 720p profile. With Boost enabled it can use the higher TV-mode rendering profile. TV mode renders up to 1080p dynamically and the system can output an upscaled 4K signal; the game itself remains capped at 30 fps.
